newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate dips to 10.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate dips to 10.7 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate dipped 50 basis points to 10.7 percent on Tuesday as lenders cut some rates amid improved liquidity of the banking sector.

The amount of kuna funds on offer grew following the central bank cut in the ratio of banks' mandatory reserve requirements. Monday's reserve payment totalled 3.42 billion kuna after a net decrease of 50 million, a bank official told Reuters.
Dealers put the daily trade on Tuesday at 32.2 million kuna against 100 million kuna supply. Fresh borrowings amounted to 16.2 million kuna, most of which was call money.
The weighted call money rate was further cut to 10.3. The rate was lowered to 10.4 percent on Monday from its usual 10.5 percent. One-month fresh loans were struck at 14 and 15 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at a steady 9.0 ercent. Banks charged between 11 and 17 percent for short and long-term old funds.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday firmer at 6.1164 against the dollar and at 3.5710 against the German mark.
